Rationale: This guidance matches a cold-start, budget-safe convolutional baseline whose main uncertainties are temporal context sufficiency and loss alignment. The architecture is intentionally simple, so the highest-value tuning axes are segment length and spectral-loss balance rather than wholesale mechanism changes.

NOTE: This implementation passes trainability checks but deviates from the proposed mathematical spec. The tuner is optimizing an approximation of the intended architecture. Deviations: The model is trainable and returns the required [B,256,T] logits. It differs from the spec in block count/dilation schedule (12 blocks with repeated [1,2,4,8,16,32] instead of 8 blocks [1..128]), but that does not break runtime.

Focus areas: Tune segmentation_size first because receptive-field usefulness and spectral-loss stability both depend on temporal context length.; Tune the spectral penalty weight before widening or deepening the stack; the memo already identifies objective mismatch as a key uncertainty.; Watch whether validation improves more from longer segments or from modest learning-rate reduction, since cold-start gated TCNs can overfit token-local structure early.; If the first run underperforms, test offline symmetric padding as the next architectural variant rather than immediately switching to attention.
Constraints: Keep predicted peak VRAM below 19 GB at baseline to preserve tuner headroom under the 24 GB operator cap.; Keep total trainable parameters below 2,000,000 for the baseline.; Use a valid segmentation_size that exactly divides 10,000,000.; Maintain batch_size small enough that skip-path activations from all residual blocks do not push memory near the cap.
Known failures: The receptive field from 8 dilated blocks may still be too short for the dominant long-period structure in files [4-9], causing oversmoothing or failure to reconstruct slow trends.; The spectral auxiliary term may overweight global magnitude matching and hurt per-timestep class accuracy, yielding better spectra but weaker denoising_score if the task metric rewards exact token reconstruction.; If segmentation_size is set much larger by the tuner, activation memory from skip paths across all residual blocks could still rise enough to reduce batch size and destabilize optimization, even though the baseline is designed to sit comfortably below the 24 GB cap.
Suggested directions: Start with segmentation_size 16000 as a conservative valid divisor that should fit easily and still expose nontrivial temporal structure.; First ablation after the baseline should keep the model fixed and vary only the spectral loss weight, since the memo explicitly proposes the registered spectral objective.; If denoising_score is weak but training is stable, extend depth from 8 to 10 blocks or switch to offline symmetric padding in the next iteration.; If spectra improve while token accuracy falls, reduce spectral weight or increase label smoothing only slightly rather than replacing the architecture.
Rationale: This guidance matches a cold-start, budget-safe convolutional baseline whose main uncertainties are temporal context sufficiency and loss alignment. The architecture is intentionally simple, so the highest-value tuning axes are segment length and spectral-loss balance rather than wholesale mechanism changes.
